summary: Port reproduces the original's Christmas-tree scene almost pixel-for-pixel in geometry (same 20-row tree, same star column, same 3-row ground, same index-only mapping) but differs in palette (much darker sky/ground, full-hue-wheel ornaments instead of the original's red+blue+silver), draws a 5-row star instead of 4, and renders snow as chunky 2-row blocks whose population swells to ~18% of the rig at peaks while the original's stays tightly regulated.
observations: DEFAULT-RIG BLOCKER: on the slug's default rig (grid 16x16, 256 px) the ORIGINAL throws 'array index out of bounds' at frame 0 (line 56) and renders pure black for the whole window, while the port renders normally (mean 71). A pixel-count sweep on the strip rig shows the original renders only when pixelCount is a multiple of 20 — OK at 20/40/60/80/100/120/200/220/240/260/300/400, 'array index out of bounds' at 50/64/144/150/210/250/256. The port has no such constraint and renders at every count tested. All judging below was therefore done on a --rig grid --grid 20x20 (400 px) override, where both sides render; the manifest rig for this slug should be changed to a 20-multiple (20x20 is the natural one: it makes both sides draw a clean, centred, correctly-proportioned tree).

Both sides are INDEX-ONLY: the flat pixel sequence at t=0 is byte-identical between --rig grid --grid 20x20 and --rig strip --pixels 400 (0/400 differing pixels on each side). Native geometry is 20 rows. At a non-square multiple of 20 (strip 300) both sides skew the scene identically, so that is shared behaviour, not a port bug.

Scene structure matches closely. At t=0 on 20x20 both draw: sky filling rows 0-16 outside the tree; a stepped triangular tree occupying row1 cols 9-10, rows 4-5 cols 7&12, row6 cols 6-13, rows 7-9 cols 4-15, rows 10-12 cols 2-17, row13 cols 1-18, rows 14-16 cols 0-19; and a 3-row solid ground band on rows 17-19 (60 px on both sides).

PALETTE, exact RGB at t=0 (orig vs port): sky [57,60,142]x150 vs [26,44,89]x147 — the port's night sky is roughly half as bright and bluer; ground/trunk [107,51,10]x60 vs [63,34,12]x60 — port ~1.7x darker; tree green [40,203,0]x126 vs [4,203,0]x114 — same value but the original's green is yellower (hue ~108 deg, i.e. the 51,255,0 family scaled by ~0.8) while the port's is near-pure green (hue ~119 deg); silver garland [152,149,122]x26 vs [127,116,89]x24 — port's tinsel is dimmer and warmer.

STAR SIZE MISMATCH: original star is 16 px = 4 rows x 4 cols (rows 2-5, cols 8-11) at [255,235,61]; port star is 20 px = 5 rows x 4 cols (rows 2-6, cols 8-11) at [255,215,76]. Confirmed by exact colour counts at t=0, t=59 and t=88 on both sides.

ORNAMENT/GARLAND HUES DIVERGE. Original decorations are only three families: silver [152,149,122], a RED run ramping [255,0,3]->[255,17,0]->[255,38,0]->[255,60,0]->[255,81,0], and a BLUE run ramping [2,0,255]->[23,0,255]->[45,0,255]->[66,0,255]->[88,0,255]. No magenta, cyan, orange or green garlands appear at any time sampled from t=0 to t=232. The port draws the same 5-px hue-ramped-run idea but across the whole hue wheel: violet/magenta [191,0,255]..[255,0,232], cyan/blue [0,92,255]..[0,195,255], green [0,255,30]..[55,255,0], orange [255,50,0]..[255,154,0], plus blue. Ornament colours are STATIC on both sides (each decoration cell holds the same RGB at t=0,5,10,15,20,25,30,40,50,59), so this is a fixed palette difference, not a phase difference.

GARLAND LAYOUT DIVERGES. Original places few, LONG runs on a few rows: silver 9 px on row8 cols5-13, silver 4 px row12 cols3-6, silver 10 px row13 cols7-16, silver 3 px row14 cols17-19; red 3 px row7 cols5-7, red 5 px row14 cols6-10; blue 5 px row9 cols11-15, blue 5 px row16 cols14-18. The port spreads roughly the same total decoration budget over MANY SHORT runs (2-4 px) scattered across rows 6-16 — e.g. silver at row7 cols5-8, row8 cols9-12, row10 cols3-5, row11 cols6-9, row12 cols10-12. Visually the original reads as horizontal garland stripes; the port reads as confetti dots.

SNOW, original: single-pixel flakes in the SAME warm tone as the star [255,235,61], fading in and out through dim values ([184,170,45], [137,127,34], [30,27,7]) so they also appear as dark specks on the sky. Typically 2-8 visible at once. Motion measured from a 20 fps dense dump (t=0..11 s): flakes drift RIGHT at ~1 px/s with sub-pixel antialiasing across two adjacent columns during transit — e.g. (row1,col12)@0.1s -> col13@0.9 -> col14@2.0 -> col15@3.0 -> col16@4.0 -> col17@5.0; independently (row3,col1)@0.2 -> col2@0.9 -> col3@2.0 -> col4@3.0 -> col5@5.0.

SNOW, port: same rightward ~1 px/s drift, but each flake is drawn as a 2-ROW-TALL x 2-4-COLUMN BLOCK, not a point (verified at t=86/87/88: identical cream runs on rows 0 AND 1 at cols 9-10 and 15-16, identical amber runs on rows 12 AND 13 at cols 6-9). Port uses TWO warm tones where the original uses one: pale cream [255,232,153] in the sky and saturated amber [255,194,38] over the tree; the original's star and snow share exactly one colour.

STEADY-STATE INSTABILITY (the biggest behavioural difference). Over a 240 s / 5 fps survey on 20x20 the original is flat: meanBrightness 87-91 (range 4), meanR 77-84 (range 7), meanG 111-120, meanB 69-73. The port swings hugely: meanBrightness 71-98 (range 27), meanR 52-101 (range 49). Sampled every 8 s, the port's amber-on-tree pixel count runs 4/19/13/11/7/8/4/12/21/21/27/32/18/24/35/23/29/31/17/15/21/8/10/15/18/14/18/20/31/30 while the original's off-star warm-pixel count stays 0-5. At the port's worst sampled moment (t=88 s) the frame is sky [26,44,89]x82, green [4,203,0]x78, pale-cream snow [255,232,153]x45, amber [255,194,38]x25, silver only x14 — i.e. ~18% of the rig is snow/amber and the sky is nearly half covered by cream bars. The original at the very same t=88 s is unchanged from t=0: sky x151, green x121, ground x60, silver x26, star x16, plus 2-4 flake pixels.

The port's sky-filling episodes recur: visible in the 240 s survey sheet at ~21.8 s, 43.6 s, 65.4 s, 87.2 s, 152.6 s, 174.4 s and 196.2 s. The original's survey sheet is visually identical at all twelve sampled times. Neither side ever dies, freezes or blacks out; both are alive at t=232 s.

MOTION RATE: over 240 s at 5 fps, orig motion avg 1.09 / motionLit 1.06 (min 0, max 2/2.4); port motion avg 0.63 / motionLit 0.67. At 20 fps over 60 s: orig 0.19/0.33, port 0.12/0.23. The port's small-scale animation is roughly half the original's — its snow blocks sit still longer — even though its long-timescale brightness drift is far larger.

No mode structure and no periodicity on either side: autocorrelation of motionLit and meanR (1200 frames, 20 fps) shows only the short-lag decay on the original (top lags 1,2,3,10 frames) and no fundamental on the port beyond noise (top lags 1, 83, 32). I specifically looked for a periodic red event (a '2 s red hold') on the original and found none — the original's meanR never leaves 77-84 across 240 s. The template-family green does show up: the original's green is the 51,255,0 family scaled ~0.8 ([40,203,0]); the port uses [4,203,0] instead. The original's grey/silver is [152,149,122], not a neutral 114,114,114.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING: not a divergence. Whole-frame temporal decorrelation measured at fps 10 vs fps 40 (corr of frame(0) with frames at 0.5/1/2/4/8 s) gives orig 0.939/0.930/0.917/0.924/0.946 at 10 fps and 0.934/0.937/0.947/0.982/0.947 at 40 fps; port 0.973/0.968/0.930/0.895/0.898 at 10 fps and 0.956/0.948/0.931/0.946/0.856 at 40 fps. Both sides decorrelate on the same SECONDS scale at both rates, so both are time-based.

SEED: judged at seeds 1, 7 and 1234 (60 s / 5 fps each on 20x20). Both sides are essentially seed-independent — the tree, star, ground and the whole decoration layout are identical across seeds on each side, and the divergences above reproduce at every seed. The port's sky-filling episodes appear at all three seeds.

CONTROLS: --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' on BOTH sides; meta.json lists controls: [] for orig and port. Control surfaces match. Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both).
feedback: Fix the ornament palette first — it is the most visible identity difference. The original decorates the tree with exactly three families: warm silver [152,149,122], a red run whose hue ramps across ~5 px from [255,0,3] to [255,81,0], and a blue run ramping from [2,0,255] to [90,0,255]. The port instead cycles the whole hue wheel (violet/magenta [191..255,0,255], cyan [0,92..195,255], green [0..55,255,0], orange [255,50..154,0]). Restrict the garland hues to red and blue plus silver.

Make the garlands long stripes, not confetti. Original run lengths at 20x20 are 3, 4, 5, 9 and 10 px on rows 7, 8, 9, 12, 13, 14 and 16 (silver 26 px total, red 8 px, blue 10 px); the port uses ~2-4 px runs scattered over rows 6-16. Fewer, longer, row-aligned runs would fix the look.

Brighten the palette: sky should be [57,60,142] (port draws [26,44,89]), ground/trunk [107,51,10] (port [63,34,12]), silver [152,149,122] (port [127,116,89]). Whole-scene mean brightness on 20x20 is 89-91 on the original vs 71-78 on the port at default seed.
Shift the tree green slightly yellower: original [40,203,0] (hue ~108 deg, the 51,255,0 family at ~0.8 scale); port draws [4,203,0] (hue ~119 deg).
Shrink the star by one row: original is 4 rows x 4 cols = 16 px on rows 2-5; port is 5 rows x 4 cols = 20 px on rows 2-6. Star colour should be [255,235,61], not [255,215,76].

Draw snowflakes as SINGLE pixels, not 2-row x 2-4-column blocks. The original's flake is one pixel wide and one row tall, antialiased across two adjacent columns only while it crosses a column boundary; the port's flake covers two full rows and several columns at once (rows 0 and 1 carry identical cream runs, rows 12 and 13 carry identical amber runs).

Use one snow colour, not two. The original's flakes are the same [255,235,61] as the star, fading in and out through dim versions ([184,170,45], [137,127,34], [30,27,7]) so they read as dark specks at the extremes. The port draws pale cream [255,232,153] in the sky and saturated amber [255,194,38] over the tree.

Cap and regulate the flake population — this is the port's worst steady-state defect. The original holds 2-8 flakes at all times over 240 s (off-star warm-pixel count 0-5 sampled every 8 s, meanBrightness 87-91, meanR 77-84). The port's warm-pixel count swings 4-45 and its meanR swings 52-101, so roughly every 20 s the sky fills with large cream bars and the tree with amber blobs (worst sampled moment t=88 s: 45 cream + 25 amber px, sky background down from 151 to 82 px). Whatever spawns and retires flakes in the port is not retiring them fast enough, and the excess is landing on the tree as amber.

Speed is right — do not change it. Both sides drift snow rightward at ~1 px/s at 20 fps and both are time-based (fps-invariant across 10/20/40). The port's lower motion stat (0.63 vs 1.09 over 240 s at 5 fps) is a consequence of the blocky, long-lived flakes, not of a wrong velocity.

Harness/manifest note for whoever fixes this: the slug's default rig (grid 16x16 = 256 px) makes the ORIGINAL error out with 'array index out of bounds' at frame 0 and render black, so the default baseline run is not judgeable. The original needs pixelCount to be a multiple of 20; 20x20 (400 px) is the natural rig and should replace 16x16 in the manifest. Also worth deciding whether the port should replicate the original's hard 20-multiple requirement or keep its current tolerance — the port renders at 50/64/144/150/210/250/256 px where the original dies.
